- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing downside momentum.
- If model shows a sharp upward spike followed by a forecast decline, it often overshoots; cap the peak at 1.2x the 14-day moving average.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a strong move, model often fails to correct; apply a 3–5 day lag correction to avoid premature reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong sentiment volatility, reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.3 to -0.4), model often fails to adjust; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days to match sentiment lag.
